name: How to Ensure Your Custom Kitchen Design Fits Perfectly

step.name: Step 1: Detailed Needs and Budget Document: Before any measurements are tak…
step.text: Detailed Needs and Budget Document: Before any measurements are taken, have a clear understanding of your lifestyle needs, aesthetic preferences, and a realistic budget. This guides the designer in creating options that are both aspirational and achievable.

step.name: Step 2: Appliance Selection and Specifications: Finalize your appliances—ma…
step.text: Appliance Selection and Specifications: Finalize your appliances—make, model, and dimensions—early in the process. Cabinetry and utility rough-ins are designed around these specifics, so changes later can be costly and cause delays. Provide these to your designer from day one.

step.name: Step 3: Accurate Site Measurements: This is paramount
step.text: Accurate Site Measurements: This is paramount. While you might take initial rough measurements, insist on professional, laser-precise measurements from your design-build team. These should account for every nuance: wall conditions, ceiling height, door and window placements, utility connections, and potential structural elements. Designs based solely on homeowner-supplied measurements are a common source of errors.
